# Act III · War Across the Water · Chapter Index and Shared Rules (SEALED — DM ONLY)

> **Act III** runs **Ch14 to Ch20**, levels **14 → 20**, about **16 sessions** (S23–S38), Thawing to Midsummer's Eve, YF 1105 (`campaign/01`).
> **Read this file first.** It holds the rules every Act III chapter uses: the Hushed in Act III, waking and laying to rest at tiers 3–4, the chain format, mass battles (the Battle Tide), the Mirror, Moss's Hart, the locket token, the ending tracks checklist and the tuning summary.
> Anything here that adds to or interprets a shared file is listed in `_change-requests.md` for the owners of those files to confirm. **Nothing here overrides `world/`, `campaign/`, `truth/` or `rules/`.** If one of those changes, it wins.
> Act II's shared rules (`act2/_index.md` §3) still apply unless this file changes them.

## 2. Act III at a glance (what has to be true at the end)
- Brannoc has turned (or Fergan rose, or the Host split), and the Pens are woken (Ch14–15). Ash can wake the deep Hushed (Ch15).
- Umbari has given the song to the three Hearkeners and died (Ch16). Mirrowen is one people (Ch16).
- The Hall of Two Rivers is open; the three paths are known; Emberford has voted on its lamps; the realm's powers are sworn (Ch17).
- The Heron is redeemed or destroyed (Ch18).
- Ommu is awake (Ch19).
- The Song is sung; the ending is decided (Ch20).

## 3. Shared rules for Act III

### 3.1 The Hushed in Act III
The Hushed template (`act2/_index.md` §3.1) is unchanged: **immune to Charmed and Frightened, resistant to psychic, vulnerable to thunder, −2 initiative (already applied in every block), never flee.** Act III's three kinds:

| Kind | Who (Act III) | Can be… |
|---|---|---|
| **Recent** | Hushed Hornbearers, Still-Herons, the Kraken-Kin, the Cistern Keeper, the Calm who fled into Highmarch's well | **Woken** by one Performance success (DC by tier, 3.2) |
| **Deep** | Ama and the Pens' calves, the deep-Hushed host at Tuskhold, the sea-giants on Ommu's shell, Walt (if still Hushed), Rook (fall branch) | **Woken** by Ash alone from Ch15 (two consecutive successes: CHG-A3-03), or the twins with one check at advantage, or the twins in a quiet scene with no roll |
| **Hushed dead** | The Gate War dead: Tuskhold's besiegers (Dunmore, the Shieldbearers, the war-mammoth), Old Varrow's knights, bell-ringer and townsfolk | **Laid to rest** at 0 HP, or by the Gate War rest-words (Religion DC 19 as an action: the creature loses its next turn; three successes lay it down), or by Lark's rest-song (Ch16 on). Never woken. Treated as Undead for spells. |

### 3.2 Waking, stirring and laying to rest (Act III DCs)
- **Waking DC:** **19 at L14–16** (tier 3) · **21 at L17–20** (tier 4) (`rules/02` tuning handoff: 15 / 17 / 19 / 21).
- **Ash's proficiency:** if CHG-A2-03 (Performance proficiency at Ch9) was accepted, it's on his sheet.
- **Help:** Bart's Help; a Luck Point; Lark humming with him (advantage); the duet (advantage, and counts double where a chain says so); the whole locket (advantage once per long rest: 3.6); Zeke speaking the Hall's words (Ch17 on: Help as a free verbal "spell" with no slot); the Blessing of the Hall (Ch17 route A: advantage on the first song check of each encounter); Saffra's Twelfth Bell (Ch14 item; doesn't stack with the locket).
- **Deep Hushed (CHG-A3-03, from Ch15):** two successful checks on consecutive turns ("holding the note"): the first *stirs*, the second *wakes*. A failure between them means start again.
- **Stirring a boss** (Vessimer, Dunmore, Omeruth): a song success makes it lose its reaction and its next legendary action (each block's *Song-Struck* trait).
- **Lark's rest-song** (Ch16 discovery): as a bonus action, she lays to rest every Hushed dead creature within 60 ft that's below half its HP. Once per fight, unless a chapter says otherwise.

### 3.3 Skill challenges as chains (Act III DCs)
Same format as Act II (`act2/_index.md` §3.3): **links**, each with two or three ways through and an automatic **lever**; **Pressure** that changes what's waiting next (never ends the story); campaign challenges (SC#5 in Ch19) keep their `campaign/02` successes-before-failures structure, run as stations.
- **DCs:** **L14–16:** easy 15, standard 17, hard 19, very hard 21. **L17–20:** easy 15, standard 17, hard 19, very hard 21 (the skill DCs plateau; the **song DCs rise to 21** at tier 4, and the stakes are what climb).
- **Reliable Talent and expertise:** Ash can't fail his expertise links. Every chain has links he can't take.
- **Social chains** (SC 16-C, 17-B, 17-C, 19-A) are mostly levers: the automatic way through is almost always *something Ash did earlier*. Read the threads table before running one.
- **Choice-only chains** (SC 20-B): no rolls; the DM judges honesty. Say so to the player.

### 3.4 Mass battles: the Battle Tide
Ch14 (Fight 22), Ch16 (Fights 27–28) and Ch20 (Fight 36) put the party in the middle of a much bigger battle. The armies are **narrative units, not stat blocks**. Track a **Battle Tide** from **−3** (the line breaks) to **+3** (the enemy breaks). Start at 0 plus the chapter's listed modifiers.
- **End of each round:** **+1** if the party met that phase's objective or saved a named unit from a named threat; **−1** if the objective went backward, a unit broke, or (Ch20) a Hearkener was downed.
- **Effects** are listed per fight: Tide gates allied damage (Ch20), fewer adds (Ch16), retreats (Ch14), and the fail-forward.
- **Discovery moments that move the Tide:** Gideon's Rally (Ch14), Gideon *leads an army* (Ch16, then once per day), Ama's song (Ch16), the gathering (Ch20).

### 3.5 The Mirror (the Stillness's signature)
Ch15 (Fight 26), Ch18 (Fight 32) and Ch20 (Fight 36) each use **the Mirror**: a Wisdom save, psychic damage, and **Stilled** (Incapacitated, speed 0: the hero sees their own still, perfect future and doesn't want to move). It deepens each time:
| Chapter | DC | Damage | Adds | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ch15 | 17 | 6d10 | Drowned Reflections (grey copies of heroes) | First time. The visions are introduced. |
| Ch18 | 19 | 8d10 | Drowned Loves (someone in each hero's vision) | Struck by its own hero, a Love is laid down. |
| Ch20 | 19 | 10d10 | Still Selves (each hero, at peace) | Struck by its own hero, a Self is gone. |
- **Not a spell, not charm.** Counterspell and Shield do nothing. **Mind Blank** stops the damage, not the Stilled. **Gideon's Aura of Warding** halves the damage (psychic resistance). **Vessimer's Blessing** (Ch18 redeemed) gives one reroll.
- **Ash's song breaks it:** an action, Performance (DC 17 in Ch15; 21 in Ch18 and 20): every Stilled ally within 120 ft is freed. Lark can do it once per fight. Clara can do it once in Ch20 for the *whole battlefield*.
- **The visions are fixed** (each character always sees the same life): Ash, his parents alive and the family whole, forever; Gideon, the night before the fire; Zeke, the Row and Hollis, before the lie; Moss, the ford and his sister young; Clara, Hester's kitchen; Lark, Gran Burdock's burrow, never growing up.

### 3.6 Moss: the Hart in Act III
- **Ch14–15 (tier 3):** if the tier-3 Hart round (Act II §3.4) wasn't spent in Ch11–13, it can be spent here. Ch15's stand against his sister is a **free scripted beat**.
- **Ch16, upgrade #4:** antlers permanently visible; **the Hart for one full round per encounter** (the full stat block is in `ch16.md`). This replaces the once-per-tier round.
- **Ch17 (Aranhollow) or Ch19 (Ommu's Rest), upgrade #5:** in the finale, **the Hart for the whole of Phase 4** (`campaign/05` §7).
- **Setback:** if the Hall is forced (Ch17 ★1 route C), Moss drops to upgrade #1 until Ch20.
- **R-012:** the Hart never attacks Vessimer. He can stand, carry, bloom and break the line around her.

### 3.9 Blessings earned in Act III (log them on the sheets)
- **The Blessing of the Hall** (Ch17, route A, passing the Ford-Warden's test): each Hearkener who sang in the Hall has advantage on the first song check of each encounter, for the rest of the campaign.
- **Vessimer's Blessing** (Ch18, redeemed): once, each party member can reroll one saving throw against a Stillness effect.
- **Ommu's Blessing** (Ch19, on waking): every party member gains Water Breathing and a swim speed equal to their walking speed, for the rest of the campaign.
